description: Imports monday.com work-management data (boards, items/pulses and their subitems, users, teams, tags) from the monday.com GraphQL API.

spec.apiVersionPinning: Request header `API-Version`, pinned to the constant "2025-07" (source_monday/graphql/constants.py). Sent explicitly on every request in execute_query and validate_credentials; not a path segment or query param.

configFields.description: ISO-8601 duration between updates for this binding. Connector-supplied defaults: PT2H for teams/users/tags, PT1H for boards/items.

configFields.name: schedule
configFields.description: Optional cron expression to automatically re-backfill this binding. Empty by default; comes from the CDK's ResourceConfigWithSchedule, not from monday-specific code.

snapshot.querySketch: Single unparameterised GraphQL document POSTed to /v2: `query { teams { id name picture_url users { id } owners { id } } }`. The executor rewrites the document to also select a top-level `complexity { query after reset_in_x_seconds }` field before sending. Records are streamed out of the response at JSON path `data.teams.item`.

GraphQL document `query ($limit: Int = 10, $page: Int = 1) { users(limit: $limit, page: $page) { ...profile fields... } }` POSTed to /v2 with variables {limit: 100, page: N}. Records streamed at JSON path `data.users.item`. The caller loops, incrementing the `page` variable, until a response yields fewer documents than `limit`.
Single unparameterised GraphQL document POSTed to /v2: `query { tags { id name color } }`. Records streamed at JSON path `data.tags.item`.

backfill.querySketch: GraphQL `query ($order_by: BoardsOrderBy = created_at, $page: Int, $limit: Int, $ids: [ID!], $state: State = all) { boards(order_by:, page:, limit:, ids:, state:) { ...full board fragment: columns, groups, owners, creator, permissions, subscribers, tags, top_group, updates, views, workspace{kind} } }` POSTed to /v2 with {limit: 100, page: N, state: "all"}. Records streamed at `data.boards.item`. On a GraphQL error the same page is retried with a fallback document that drops the `workspace` selection, then with binary-search chunking over board IDs. Emitted boards are filtered client-side to `updated_at <= cutoff` and `state != deleted`.

incremental.querySketch: Three-phase, per-invocation window [log_cursor, min(log_cursor + 2h, now - 5m)]. (1) Enumerate every board id/state/updated_at with `query ($limit: Int = 10000, $page: Int = 1, $state: State = all) { boards(limit:, page:, state:, order_by: created_at) { id name state updated_at } }`, paged on `page` until an empty page. (2) For those board ids, `query ($start: ISO8601DateTime!, $end: ISO8601DateTime!, $ids: [ID!]!, $limit: Int!, $activity_limit: Int!, $page: Int) { boards(ids:, limit:, page:, order_by: created_at) { id state updated_at activity_logs(from: $start, to: $end, limit: $activity_limit) { account_id created_at data entity event id user_id } } }` in batches of 500 boards x 100 logs, paged on `page` until a page yields no logs. Activity-log events are mapped to board-changed / board-deleted. (3) Re-fetch the changed board ids with the full board document in chunks of 100. Deleted boards are emitted with _meta.op = 'd'. Cursor advances to max(change timestamp)+1s, or to window_end when nothing changed.

paginator.limitParam: limit (GraphQL variable; 10000 for the id sweep, len(board_ids) for the activity-log query)

backfill.querySketch: Board-partitioned. The page cursor is a JSON object mapping still-unprocessed board id -> false; boards are removed with a JSON merge patch {board_id: null} as they complete, 10 boards per fetch_page call. Board ids are seeded from the minimal-boards sweep (excluding deleted boards). Per board: `query GetBoardItems($boardIds: [ID!]!, $boardsLimit: Int, $boardsPage: Int, $itemsLimit: Int, $state: State = all) { boards(ids:, limit:, page:, state:, order_by: created_at) { id state updated_at items_page(limit: $itemsLimit) { cursor items { ...ItemFields } } } }` with boardsLimit 1 and itemsLimit 5. Items stream at `data.boards.item.items_page.items.item`; the `items_page.cursor` from the response envelope is then fed to `query GetNextItems($cursor: String!, $limit: Int) { next_items_page(limit:, cursor:) { cursor items { ...ItemFields } } }` (limit 100), looping while a cursor is returned. Subitem `state` is backfilled separately via `items(ids:)` in batches of 100 because requesting it inline 500s. Emitted items are filtered to `updated_at <= cutoff` and `state != deleted`.

paginator.cursorBodyKey: variables.cursor (GraphQL variable on the next_items_page query)

incremental.querySketch: Same windowing as boards ([log_cursor, min(log_cursor + 2h, now - 5m)]). Enumerate non-deleted board ids, pull `activity_logs(from:, to:, limit: 100)` for them in batches of 500 boards (paged on `page` until a page yields no logs), and classify each event into item-changed / item-deleted / full-board-item-refresh. Changed item ids are re-read with `query GetItemsByIds($ids: [ID!]!, $limit: Int, $page: Int) { items(ids:, limit:, page:) { ...ItemFields } }` in chunks of 100 ids, up to 5 chunk queries concurrently; results outside the window are dropped. Boards flagged for full refresh are re-read through the GetBoardItems / next_items_page cursor walk. Deleted items are emitted with _meta.op = 'd'. Cursor advances to max(activity-log created_at)+1s, else to window_end.

paginator.limitParam: limit (GraphQL variable, set to the batch's board count)

authTierRationale: The shipped EndpointConfig exposes exactly one credential option: the CDK's `AccessToken` model, whose only required field is a single secret `access_token` string titled "Private App Credentials". A monday.com user generates this themselves from their account's Developer/Admin API area; no app registration and no refresh token are involved. The CDK's TokenSource returns the token verbatim and the HTTP layer sends it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (DEFAULT_AUTHORIZATION_HEADER / DEFAULT_AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN_TYPE), and `TokenSource(oauth_spec=None, ...)` confirms no OAuth exchange occurs at runtime. An `OAUTH2_SPEC` for provider "monday" (authorization_code grant against auth.monday.com) is defined in models.py but is deliberately NOT wired into EndpointConfig — an in-code TODO says OAuth2Credentials will be added only once monday.com approves Estuary's public OAuth app. So today the standalone tier is T1 and there is no T2/T3 alternative.

unionMisfits.description: This is a single-endpoint GraphQL connector. There is no per-stream path: every stream, every page, and every retry is a POST to the same https://api.monday.com/v2 URL with a different GraphQL document in the JSON body. The schema's `http` PullSpec (path/recordsPath/params) has no meaningful content here, so all five streams use `kind: "query"` with `language: "other"`. `recordsPath` is nonetheless a real and load-bearing concept in this connector (the CDK streams records out of a JSON path such as `data.boards.item.items_page.items.item`), but the `query` PullSpec has no field for it, so it is folded into querySketch.

proposedShape.recordsPath: str (JSON path the records are streamed from)

unionMisfits.description: The items backfill has TWO nested pagination mechanisms operating at once and the Paginator union can express only one. Outer: a board-partitioned resumable cursor that is a JSON object {board_id: false} mutated by JSON merge patch {board_id: null} on completion — this is neither offset, page, nor a token; it is a work-queue checkpoint held in connector state. Inner: the opaque monday `items_page.cursor` -> `next_items_page(cursor:)` walk, which is what is recorded in the emitted paginator. The recorded paginator therefore describes only the inner leg.

proposedShape.seededBy: str (how the queue is initially enumerated)
proposedShape.checkpointEncoding: str (e.g. JSON merge patch, key -> null on completion)

unionMisfits.description: The incremental leg is not a filtered re-read of the resource; it is a change-feed read from a *different* GraphQL field (`activity_logs` hung off each board) whose events are decoded into board/item ids that are then re-fetched with a second query. It behaves like `kind: "changes"` (it emits real deletes via _meta.op='d' and has a retention limit) but rides the polling HTTP path, so neither `changes` nor `query` fits cleanly.

proposedShape.eventSource: str (the field/endpoint the change events come from)

unionMisfits.description: `continuity` is documented as required only for mode "log", and this connector is mode "poll", so it is emitted as null. But there IS a real our-side loss here: monday.com retains only ~10k activity logs per board, and the connector's own comments say a stalled cursor risks logs being purged between sync cycles (it deliberately advances the cursor to window_end even when nothing changed, to mitigate this). A poll-mode connector reading a bounded-retention change feed has genuine resume-window risk that the current shape gives it nowhere to record.

abstained.credentialModes[1]: An OAUTH2_SPEC for provider "monday" (authUrl https://auth.monday.com/oauth2/authorize, tokenUrl https://auth.monday.com/oauth2/token, authorization_code grant, access token read from /access_token) is fully defined in source_monday/models.py:38-63, and an OAuth2Credentials alias is built from it under TYPE_CHECKING. It is NOT referenced by EndpointConfig and TokenSource is constructed with oauth_spec=None, so it is dead code today; an in-code TODO says it will be enabled only once monday.com approves the OAuth app. Listing it as an offered credential mode would misstate what a user can actually configure, so it is recorded here instead. Note also that no `scopes` list appears anywhere in the connector, so even if it were live the scope set could not be recovered.
abstained.credentialModes[0].scheme.prefix: The connector never sets an explicit header or token-type prefix; it relies on the CDK defaults (DEFAULT_AUTHORIZATION_HEADER = "Authorization", DEFAULT_AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN_TYPE = "Bearer"), so the wire format is `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Recorded as scheme type "bearer", but note this is a CDK default rather than a monday-specific decision, and monday.com is known to also accept the bare token — the connector code itself does not state which form is required.
abstained.execution.continuity: The schema makes `continuity` required only for mode "log"; this connector is mode "poll" and leaves no server-side artifacts on monday.com (no slot, no consumer group, no scratch object — every read is a stateless POST). It is therefore emitted as null. See unionMisfits[3]: there IS a genuine our-side loss (monday's ~10k-activity-logs-per-board retention) that the poll shape gives no place to record.
abstained.discovery: streamMode is static: the five bindings are hard-coded lists in resources.py and `discover` simply returns all_resources(). The connector does not inspect the customer's schema, so there is no discovery method, query, exclude list, or allowlist to report.
abstained.streams[3].pull.incremental.paginator.pa: Recorded as 10000 (the minimal-board-enumeration limit), but the incremental leg issues two differently-paged queries in one invocation: the board-id sweep uses limit 10000, while the activity-log query sets limit to the batch's board count (up to 500) with a separate activity_limit of 100 per board. The single Paginator slot cannot express both; treat the recorded pageSize as the enumeration leg only.
abstained.streams[4].pull.incremental.paginator: Marked low confidence. The items incremental leg's outer pagination is the activity-log board batching (500 boards/batch, page variable, terminating when a page yields no logs), which is what is recorded. But the re-fetch of changed item ids is not paginated at all — it is chunked client-side into groups of 100 ids with page fixed at 1 — and the full-board-refresh path re-enters the items_page/next_items_page cursor walk. Three distinct mechanisms in one leg; the recorded paginator describes only the activity-log sweep.
abstained.streams[*].cursorField: For boards and items, `updated_at` is what the emitted documents carry and what the backfill cutoff compares against, so it is recorded as the cursor field. But the incremental log cursor is NOT advanced from document `updated_at` in the general case — it is advanced from the max activity-log `created_at` (a 17-digit monday-specific timestamp, parsed by source_monday/utils.py), and falls back to window_end when no changes are seen. The items code comments explicitly that board-level refreshes emit items whose `updated_at` may be years old without moving the cursor. So `updated_at` is the document's change marker, not strictly the state cursor.
abstained.streams[0..2].supportedSyncModes: teams/users/tags are opened with fetch_snapshot plus a tombstone document, i.e. the whole collection is re-read each interval and rows absent from the new snapshot are tombstoned. Recorded as full_refresh + snapshot_with_tombstone. There is no incremental variant and no cursor field for these three.
